tasks.short: Note ingredient lots and weights, temperatures and cycle times, record test results, type the batch sheet into the spreadsheet and check the record for gaps.

steps.what: Batchmaker writes ingredient lots and weights on the batch sheet
Batchmaker records temperature and time cycle from the mixer display
Batchmaker records test results for each food product batch
Batchmaker types the batch sheet into the production spreadsheet
Batchmaker checks the batch record for gaps and out-of-spec values

tasks.design: The weighing station scans each ingredient's lot and sends weights to the batch record in the production system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), and the mixer logs temperatures and cycle times there itself. Test instruments send results to the same record, and a batch view flags missing entries and out-of-spec values for the batchmaker to check. No batch sheet is retyped.
tasks.previous_blocker: Lots, weights, temperatures and test results were written on paper and retyped.
tasks.enabler_now: Weighing stations, mixer controls and test instruments can send data to production systems.
tasks.still_hard: Older mixers and hand tests still need manual entry.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a batch smells wrong even though the numbers are fine.
tasks.altitude: The batchmaker checks flagged values instead of writing records.

reach.learn: Whether complete records speed up release.

evidence.claim: Weighing stations, mixer controls and test instruments can send data to production systems.
Food businesses must trace one step back and one step forward and hand over records without undue delay.

assumptions: Boundary: from weighed ingredients to the checked batch record; batch release is outside.
Input contract: lots from supplier labels; spec limits set by the quality officer; fallback is paper batch sheets.
Checking flagged values still needs a person.
Records show batches, not individual workers.
research_questions: Do record gaps at audit fall?

incremental.description: Batchmaker enters values when an instrument link fails.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older mixers do not log and some weighing stations lack a lot scanner, so temperatures, cycles and many lots are still written (39.0); high: all stations and mixers linked (73.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Brief helpers on the day's batches, direct them during mixing, correct mistakes and post the batch list.

steps.what: Batchmaker briefs helpers on the day's batches
Batchmaker gives directions to other workers assisting in the batchmaking process
Batchmaker corrects helpers' mistakes on the line
Batchmaker writes the day's batch list on the whiteboard

tasks.design: A screen at the line shows the day's batches and their order from the production plan ({OPS_SYSTEM}), so the whiteboard goes and the briefing is shorter. Directing and correcting helpers stay with the batchmaker.
tasks.previous_blocker: The batch list was written on a whiteboard and explained in full each morning.
tasks.enabler_now: Production systems drive line screens from the plan.
tasks.still_hard: Changes during the shift are still passed on by voice.
tasks.human_edge: Showing a new helper how dough should feel when it is ready.

reach.learn: Whether line screens cut wrong-order batches.

evidence.claim: Production systems can show the day's batch plan on line screens.
Ranking staff on system logins is personnel monitoring that needs works council consent where a council exists.

assumptions: Boundary: from the production plan to corrected work; planning itself is outside.
Input contract: production plan from the planner; fallback is the whiteboard.
Directing and correcting keep their full time. s1 keeps 90 because only reading out the batch list goes; the briefing on the day's work stays.
Helpers' time is outside the batchmaker's savings.

incremental.description: Batchmaker checks the line screen at shift start.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the plan changes during the day and the screen lags, so the whiteboard and full briefing partly return (2.0); high: the screen follows the plan (7.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Pick ingredients by the recipe, check labels and lots, scale the recipe to the batch size, weigh ingredients on balance scales and record actual weights.

steps.what: Batchmaker selects ingredients from the store by the recipe
Batchmaker checks ingredient labels against the recipe sheet
Batchmaker calculates quantities for the batch size
Batchmaker weighs ingredients on balance scales using metric measures
Batchmaker notes actual weights on the weighing list

tasks.design: The recipe system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) scales the recipe to the batch size, and a guided weighing station shows each target weight and tolerance and blocks an ingredient whose scanned code does not match the recipe. Actual weights go to the batch record by themselves. Picking and weighing stay with the batchmaker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Quantities were worked out on paper and labels checked by eye.
tasks.enabler_now: Guided weighing stations scan ingredients and show targets and tolerances.
tasks.still_hard: Small additions and odd containers still need care at the scale.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a sack has been opened and may be damp.

reach.learn: Whether scanning catches mix-ups earlier in the store.

evidence.claim: Aptean Bakery ERP keeps formulas, flags allergens and shows cost per product.
A new or changed recipe must update the allergen information for consumers.

assumptions: Boundary: from the recipe to the weighing list; mixing is outside.
Input contract: recipes kept by the product developer; ingredient codes on supplier labels; fallback is paper.

incremental.description: Batchmaker checks scale calibration at shift start.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: guided weighing only on the main line, so labels are still read and weights noted for the rest (20.0); high: guided stations on every line (31.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the recipe's mixing steps, decide the mixing sequence, check ingredient temperatures, adjust when ingredients behave differently and note changes for the next batch.

steps.what: Batchmaker reads the mixing instructions in the recipe folder
Batchmaker determines mixing sequences based on temperature effects and solubility
Batchmaker probes ingredient temperatures before adding them
Batchmaker adjusts the sequence when ingredients behave differently
Batchmaker notes changes to the sequence for the next batch: in the recipe folder today, on the mixer screen where the product developer reads them after the change

tasks.design: The mixer screen shows the recipe's mixing steps from the recipe system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) and live temperatures from probes in the tanks, so less probing by hand is needed. The batchmaker notes changes to the sequence on the same screen, an ordinary save that the product developer reads. Deciding and adjusting the sequence stay with the batchmaker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mixing steps were in a paper folder and temperatures probed by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Mixer screens show recipe steps and probe readings.
tasks.still_hard: Raw material variation still needs the batchmaker's feel.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing to add the sugar later on a hot day.

evidence.claim: Mixer screens can show recipe steps and live probe temperatures.
Records of production must support tracing food one step back and one step forward.

assumptions: Boundary: from the recipe to sequence notes; recipe approval is outside.
Input contract: recipes kept by the product developer; probe readings from the mixer; fallback is the paper folder.
Deciding, adjusting and noting changes keep their full time; the note is a first record. s1 keeps 70 for reading the steps on screen; s3 keeps 60 for probing ingredients the tank probes do not cover.
Product developers' time is outside the batchmaker's savings.

incremental.description: Batchmaker cleans and checks the tank probes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: probes in only some tanks, so most temperatures are still probed by hand (8.5); high: probes in all tanks (13.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The batchmaker keeps mixing judgement, weighing and directing helpers; paper batch sheets, retyping and hand calculations shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A batchmaker whose batch record is complete when the batch is done.
